title: Add golden tests + fixtures for streaming tool-call sequences
author: Sabrina James
body: Summary: Adds golden transcript tests for streaming tool-calling in the Python SDK to lock down the canonical event model used across docs/examples. These tests validate (a) partial tool-call argument deltas, (b) correct final tool-call assembly, (c) tool-result message injection, and (d) error branches for truncated/disconnected streams. Motivation: We’ve seen repeated regressions and user confusion around partial tool-call args mid-stream (see SUP-18421). The examples refresh work requires stable, cross-language behavior; these tests provide a guardrail and a source of truth for fixture payload shape. What’s included: - New pytest suite that replays recorded streaming event sequences (“golden transcripts”) through the same consumer logic used by examples. - Fixtures that cover: single tool call, parallel tool calls (multiple tool_call_ids), and an interrupted stream where tool args arrive in multiple chunks. - Output normalization to prevent flakes: strips request_id, timestamps, and nondeterministic IDs; stable ordering for parallel tool call assembly; and line-ending normalization for CI parity. - Developer workflow for updating fixtures: set UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 to regenerate transcripts locally (documented below). CI notes: Golden tests intentionally avoid live API calls. We record fixtures once and then replay them. This keeps CI reliable and removes dependency on model variability. There is still a small risk of flake if JSON key ordering changes in serialization; the normalizer now canonicalizes JSON before comparison. How to run: - pytest -k golden_streaming_tool_calls - To update fixtures: UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 pytest -k golden_streaming_tool_calls Notes / gotchas: - These tests assert payload-shape and assembly semantics, not model content quality. - The fixtures include partial args segments to mirror real-world streaming behavior; do not “simplify” them into one chunk, otherwise we regress the exact failure mode we’re guarding. - If the event model changes, please coordinate with ENG-4826 (docs) and the TS/Go fixtures to keep parity.
commits: test(streaming): add golden harness for streaming tool-call events
test(fixtures): add recorded transcripts for tool-calls + parallel calls
test(util): normalize ids/timestamps + canonicalize JSON to reduce flakes
docs(testing): add README notes for updating goldens
files_changed: redwood/_internal/streaming/assemble.py (small refactor: expose helper used by tests)
.github/workflows/ci.yml (ensure golden tests run in unit job)
conversation: Ibrahim Khan: The fixture approach looks good. Two asks: (1) ensure we normalize tool_call_id only when it’s clearly nondeterministic; we still want to assert that the same id is used across deltas within a call. (2) Add one case that includes partial JSON args that only become valid at the end (mirrors SUP-18421).

Sabrina James (author): Updated normalizer to preserve per-call tool_call_id consistency (we only strip request_id / timestamps / trace ids). Added tool_calls_partial_args.jsonl fixture where args are invalid JSON until the last delta and we assert assembly results in valid JSON.
Sahana Iyer: CI flake risk: are we relying on dict ordering for JSON comparisons? We’ve had cross-platform diffs on this before. Recommend canonicalization + stable dumps.
Sabrina James (author): Good catch. Added canonical_json() that sorts keys and removes whitespace for comparisons. Also normalized \r\n to \n when reading fixtures.

Brian Murphy: Please add a brief comment in the test explaining that we’re validating event semantics (ordering + assembly) rather than model output. Otherwise future readers will try to “fix” the fixture content.
Sabrina James (author): Added comments + expanded tests/golden/README.md to clarify intent and update procedure.
Monica Patel: Approving contingent on one more thing: add a marker so these can be run separately (fast) and don’t slow down the full suite too much.
Sabrina James (author): Added pytest -m golden marker and wired into CI under unit-tests; it’s ~0.6s locally.
Ibrahim Khan: LGTM. This unblocks ENG-4823/ENG-4826 parity work.
release_notes: N/A (tests/fixtures only; no user-facing API change)
